result.summary: PR #207 (KNOWN0, Qwen) does what the brief asks. It adds 52 lines to scripts/rules/Knowledge.gd: the three constants, plus share_gone, known, known_share, pip_of and shown, in the order the brief sets. It adds 207 lines to tests/knowledge_test.gd: 13 new _check calls, for 24 in all. The existing 11 checks and the print line are unchanged; the diff only adds lines. The maths is right. share_gone is measured on start minus FLOOR, so Body at exposure 18 reads exactly 0.6. Every boundary uses EPS. Fire from sparring alone stops at 12.5/24.5 = 0.51, and stale is untouched. I worked every boundary case by hand: 17.9/29.9 = 0.5987 is not known, 18 is known, 59.95/71.95 = 0.83322 sits under 5/6 - EPS = 0.83323, and 13c averages 0.4, giving pip 2. All of them come out the way the brief expects. None of the new checks can only pass. Check 16, check 11, check 15a (it fails if shown just hands back range_of) and checks 10a/10d would each turn red on the trap the brief names. I found no fudge factor and no loosened bar, and no files outside OWNS changed. No tools/ or docs/ files were added. The PR body shows 24 checks for knowledge and the pronoun test passing in the dispatcher's headless run. CI was cancelled at 24 min with no test failing, and I could not run Godot here. Neither file has changed on main since the merge base 48e9d409, so the diff applies cleanly. REST1 (6fa2b52b) touched only scripts/rules/Attrs.gd and tests/rest_keeps_stamina_test.gd. Knowledge.gd preloads Attrs.gd but none of the new code uses it. Four small gaps remain, all in the test file or the PR text: the test file is 492 lines, over the brief's 450 cap but under the 500 rule; test 15 declares `var s` twice; check 12 asserts share_gone 1.0 for Body only; and the PR body leaves out the share_gone paste the brief asked for. It is safe to merge as is. The fixes are cleanup.

problems.issue: _test15_shown declares `var s: Dictionary` in two sibling loops (15a and 15b). The brief forbids reusing a name in new code, and GDSCRIPT_TRAPS.md:4 calls it a parse error. It compiles today (the dispatcher's run was green), but it breaks the rule.
problems.fix: Rename the 15a loop variable to `s_known` (and its uses on the next lines) and the 15b one to `s_open`.

problems.issue: Check 12 asserts share_gone 1.0 for the all_seen k only on body; the brief says share_gone 1.0 for all three groups.
problems.fix: Add `ok = ok and absf(K.share_gone(k_all, "skills") - 1.0) < 0.0001 and absf(K.share_gone(k_all, "fire") - 1.0) < 0.0001` before the _check (typed via locals if preferred).

problems.issue: The test file is 492 lines, over the brief's 450-line cap (still under the 500 hard rule). Test 11 repeats the body and skills blocks almost word for word.
problems.fix: Fold test 11 into one inner `for grp in ["body", "skills"]` loop with per-group prev values in a Dictionary, which saves about 15 lines. Or accept 492 as under the 500 rule.

problems.issue: An unreachable guard `if start <= FLOOR: return 0.0` that the brief did not ask for. It is harmless (GROUPS has only three groups, all with start > FLOOR) and is not a fudge.
problems.fix: Leave it or delete the two lines; no behaviour change either way.

problems.issue: The PR body leaves out the share_gone paste the brief asked for (Body at 3/8/18/36/60 and Fire after 12.5 spar = 0.51).
problems.fix: No code fix. When collecting, note in the commit message that the values follow e/(e+12): 0.2/0.4/0.6/0.75/0.833, and Fire spar-only 0.510.

missed: The test file's header comment (tests/knowledge_test.gd:2-10) still lists only tests 1-9. Tests 10-16 are not described there. This is cosmetic only.

Nothing tests shown() branch (a), an attribute outside GROUPS such as 'potential', which should give range_of's exact answer with known true. The brief lists no check for it, so the PR does not break the contract, but the branch has no coverage.

Check 16's first half (wrong_measure < 0.6) depends only on width() and BODY_START, so it is fixed and cannot fail through share_gone. Only its second half (sg >= 0.6 - EPS at exposure 18) catches the trap, and 10a already checks that. It still meets the brief as written.

The PR body has no explicit line showing the test red on main; it lists only the RESULT lines. Reading the code confirms the red: the merge base has no known/share_gone/pip_of/shown, so the test cannot compile there.
